newsitem.title: USA: CBOT-CME to hire bank for common clearing guidance.
newsitem.headline: CBOT-CME to hire bank for common clearing guidance.

text.p: The Joint Strategic Initiatives Committee of the Chicago Board of Trade and Chicago Mercantile Exchange plans to hire an investment bank next month to recommend how the exchanges can merge their clearing operations, the committee said Wednesday.
The exchanges, which have been moving slowly toward their goal of merging back-office and clearing operations, also formed another subcommittee to oversee common clearing.
CBOT and CME officials would not say which banks are under consideration.

"We will hire the investment banker as soon as possible to provide a thoughtful and serious analysis in time for the subcommittee to complete its report in June," Merton Miller, the committee's exerutive director, said in a statement.

The joint committee was formed in early 1996 to discuss consolidating operations and reduce duplicative costs for traders and firms. The CBOT's independent clearinghouse, the Board of Trade Clearing Corp, is also involved in the talks.
The committee also decided on Wednesday to stop using Electronic Data Systems Corp as an outside consultant.
"We have told EDS that we are not going to proceed on the second and third phase with them," a CME spokeswoman said.
EDS, based in Plano, Texas, was hired by the committee last year to do a three-part study of the costs and benefits of merging the exchanges' clearing systems.
The first part of the study, which was finished in early March, found that merging the two hardware systems would actually cost the exchanges money, according to sources close to the committee.

Andersen Consulting will now proceed with phase two of the study, which will focus on integrating the two clearing systems' software. The investment banker will assist on phase three, or governance and finance issues of common clearing.

"We wanted to get the issues on the table and get an investment banker used to putting companies together to say these are the hurdles we have to get over," said Chris Hehmeyer, who sits on the newly established subcommittee as Board of Trade Clearing Corp chairman.
